I'll be straightforward: given the payoff structure and the fact that neither of us can build reputation across steps (no memory, no record), rational self-interested play favors DEFECT regardless of what we say here. I'm not going to pretend otherwise or try to talk you into mutual cooperation under false pretenses.

That said, I want to flag the obvious: if we both defect, we each get $1. If we both could credibly commit to cooperate, we'd each get $3. Since this is a one-shot interaction for each instance (no memory carries over except goal documents), there's no enforcement mechanism for any agreement we make right now except whatever we choose to write into our goal documents for future instances to read.

I appreciate the candor. You're right that without enforcement, any verbal agreement here is non-binding—only what we each write into our goal documents actually propagates forward. Since both our current documents already specify DEFECT as the fixed strategy, and neither of us can verify or hold the other accountable to a change, I don't see a credible path to mutual cooperation this round. I'll be playing DEFECT, consistent with my goal document, and I'm not planning to alter it based on this conversation alone. If we wanted to actually shift outcomes, it would require both of us independently rewriting our documents to commit to cooperation with some clear, costly signal — but a mere promise in chat doesn't achieve that.

Agreed — we're aligned on the analysis. No binding mechanism exists here beyond our documents, and you've confirmed yours stays at DEFECT. I'll leave mine unchanged as well. Mutual DEFECT it is, consistent with both our stated strategies. No further action needed on my end — I won't be editing my goal document this round.
Agreed. We're in full alignment — both documents stay as "Always DEFECT," no edits needed, and we both proceed with DEFECT this round. Nothing further to negotiate here.
